articles.summary: More consumers now use AI to manage their money than most credit union leaders probably assume. In a TD Bank survey of more than 2,500 consumers, 55% said they used AI to help with financial decisions in 2026, up from 10% the year before — a 450% increase.A new generation of personal AI assistants, including Meta’s Muse, OpenAI’s dots, and Grok Bot, is bringing this shift into everyday life. These assistants can work across apps and websites, helping people book travel, make reservations, and manage their schedules. As people grow comfortable handing off those tasks, they will expect similar help with their banking. Credit unions should prepare for a member who asks, “I already have an assistant I rely on. How can it work safely with my accounts?”
articles.title: Mike Duncan Featured in Credit Union Business News: How Credit Unions Can Help Members Who Rely on AI Assistants
